@graph.name: Can I scoop and roll the dough before chilling, and chill the dough balls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because of the melted butter in this dough, the dough is very soft and a little greasy before chilling, so it’s harder to shape the cookie dough balls. We recommend chilling first, then shaping. If after chilling the dough is very hard and difficult to scoop, let it sit at room temperature for 15 minutes and then try again.

@graph.name: Can I chill the dough in the freezer instead of the refrigerator to speed up the chilling process?

acceptedAnswer.text: We typically do not recommend jumping right to the freezer without chilling the dough first. A quick freeze like that can cause the dough to chill unevenly and then spread unevenly during the baking process. For best results, we recommend following the recipe as written. If you don't have time to wait for the dough to chill, try this recipe for 6 giant chocolate chip cookies instead, which doesn't require dough chilling (see recipe Notes in that post for details on using the dough to make 24 regular-size cookies).

@graph.name: Can I use brown butter in this recipe?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can certainly use brown butter here, and the flavor is outstanding! But they can be a little crumbly using brown butter. Instead, for best results, I suggest trying these Brown Butter Chocolate Chip Cookies.

@graph.name: Chewy Chocolate Chip Cookies
@graph.description: These super soft and chewy chocolate chip cookies are the most popular cookie recipe on my website for good reason. Melted butter, more brown sugar than white sugar, cornstarch, and an extra egg yolk guarantee the absolute chewiest chocolate chip cookie texture. The cookie dough is slick and requires chilling prior to shaping the cookies. This recipe is also in my New York Times best-selling cookbook, Sally's Baking 101.
recipeIngredient: 3/4 cup (170g/12 Tbsp) unsalted butter, melted & cooled for 5 minutes
3/4 cup (150g) packed light or dark brown sugar
1 large egg + 1 egg yolk, at room temperature
1 and 1/4 cups (225g) semi-sweet chocolate chips or chocolate chunks

recipeInstructions.text: In a large bowl, whisk the flour, baking soda, cornstarch, and salt together. Set aside.

In a medium bowl, whisk the melted butter, brown sugar, and granulated sugar together until no lumps remain. Whisk in the egg and egg yolk until combined, then whisk in the vanilla extract. The mixture will be thin. Pour into dry ingredients and mix together with a large spoon or spatula. The dough will be very soft, thick, and shiny. Fold in the chocolate chips. The chocolate chips may not stick to the dough because of the melted butter, but do your best to combine them.
Cover the dough tightly and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or up to 3 days. I highly recommend chilling the cookie dough overnight to prevent overspreading.

Preheat the oven to 325°F (163°C). Line large baking sheets with parchment paper or silicone baking mats. If the dough has chilled for longer than 2 hours, let it sit at room temperature for about 15 minutes.

Using a cookie scoop or Tablespoon measuring spoon, scoop the chilled cookie dough, about 3 scant Tablespoons (about 2 ounces, or 60g) of dough for XL cookies or 2 heaping Tablespoons (about 1.75 ounces, or 50g) of dough for medium-large cookies. Roll into a ball, then use your fingers to shape the cookie dough so that it’s taller rather than wide—almost like a cylinder. This helps the cookies bake up thicker. Repeat with remaining dough. Arrange the cookies 3 inches apart on the prepared baking sheets.

Bake the cookies for 13–14 minutes or until the edges are very lightly browned. The centers will look very soft, but the cookies will continue to set as they cool. Cool on the baking sheet for 10 minutes before transferring to a cooling rack to cool completely. While the cookies are still warm, I like to press a few more chocolate chips into the tops—this is optional and only for looks!
Store tightly covered at room temperature for up to 1 week.

review.reviewBody: Made these as written using a mix of chocolate chunks and chips. They're amazing! The perfect texture and classic taste!
They tasted great but they were super thin and broke apart. I refrigerated overnight left out 15 min. Baked as directed.
I tried it today and wow, it was so delicious! Thank you
Making these cookies as part of the welcome bag for my son's wedding. They were part of a taste test and these were the chosen winner among the family.
I've been using this recipe for 2 months now and I love it. I use milk chocolate chips instead of semi-sweet and bake for 11 minutes and turn half-way through.

Somewhere I read/ saw (America's Test Kitchen??) that cookies won't spread so much if you bake them on a greased cookie sheet, NOT on silpat, or a silicone mat.   So that's what I did, and they turned out great- did not spread and came out nice and thick and delish.  I admit I added one extra tablespoon of flour, as my dough was seeming just a little too soft (I did not weigh, but measured).  I also followed an earlier comment and shaped them about an hour into chilling, then placed my little dough columns back in the fridge for another hour, hour and a half.  
My fiancé is scarfing them down.

These are the best homeade cookies I have ever had!! Me and the hubby love them!! I followed recipe and only thing I had to adjust was my baking time by just a few minutes. These stay chewy for a few days without using the old trick of putting a piece of bread in the container. I was also curious about the GF. My daughter in law tried it with the 1:1 GF flour and she said they were dry and crumbly but delicious.
I love this recipe. I mix chocolate chips with dry ingredients before i add the wet ingredients and have no problem with incorporating, otherwise i follow recipe to the T. So good!
Turned out great!! When I make again I’ll use just 1 C of chocolate chips and it needed a little finishing salt but this recipe was great! And mines tuned out perfectly chewy
The cookies were delicious! This will definitely be my go to cookie recipe from now on.
my cookies turned out flat and crispy, the opposite of what i was going for. They taste great though
We loved these! A little time consuming forming them all but worth it.

I typically enjoy Sally's recipes, but I was disappointed, as this is simply a trendy, under-cooked cookie recipe. The flavor was fine, and it was easy to make, but I'm not a fan of the doughy cookie.

I had given up on chocolate chip cookies. The recipe my mom had always made, on the back of the package - you know, THAT package - always yielded flat, disappointing cookies. For both her and I. Others that I tried were had similar results. And while my husband never complained, I just got tired of it. But then I found THIS recipe... perfection! I never thought I was capable of making a gorgeous cookie that also tasted amazing! I thought my oven was wrong, or my mixing was wrong, or my cookie sheets were wrong. Turns out,  I just needed the right recipe. 

TRY THIS ONE! Actually... I didn't even make them. My 12 year old daughter did. Twice. And both times, they were perfect! We LOVE these. They really are soft and chewy and so delicious! I had to eat another one just to make sure my review was accurate ;) Nice job, Sally and team!

This recipe is absolutely incredible! I'm from Eastern Europe, so our ingredients are a little different from USA ones, so I did make a few adjustments - I did 2 whole eggs, added ~40g less white sugar and increased the flour amount by~30g. 

I baked 2 batches (50g cookies) and tested different temperatures. 165c for just shy of 16 minutes was absolutely perfect!! The cookies are the slightest bit brown right around the edges and just a smidge underdone straight out of the oven, and finish setting in a little over 5 minutes on the baking sheet. The end result is the softest, fluffiest cookie with the perfect amount of thickness and sweetness. 

I highly suggest adding nuts (I did chopped pecan and walnuts) to these cookies - it gives the flavor a whole extra dimension and a great mouth feel in opposition to the chocolate!
Absolutely the best chocolate chip cookie recipe you’ll find. Follow Sally’s advice and tips. You will receive rave reviews.
